author: Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump’s campaign to reshape the federal workforce has left in its wake demoralized employees who have lost confidence in their ability to do their jobs, according to a new survey by the Partnership for Public Service.
title: Federal Workers Say They Are Demoralized and Less Engaged Under Trump

description: Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi sat down with President Trump amid the Iran War and rising global gas prices. Mario Parker breaks down what you need to know from the nation's capital. Watch "The Debrief with Mario Parker" only on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power" (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Debrief with Mario Parker: Japan Prime Minister, Rising Gas Prices

description: Former US Defense Secretary Leon Panetta discusses the rationale for additional supplemental funding amid ongoing operations in Iran, the challenges of replenishing US military supplies, and the strategy required to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He also addresses the potential need for sustained military presence, including air and possible ground operations, and the broader economic and political implications of the conflict. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Panetta on War Costs, Hormuz Strategy, US Role

description: Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan, Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security Committee and member of the Armed Services Committee, discusses the prospect of a $200 billion supplemental request from the Pentagon, questions around military strategy and readiness, and the potential for US escalation in Iran. He also addresses the DHS funding standoff and his opposition to the nomination of Markwayne Mullin to lead the department. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Peters on War Funding, DHS, Mullin Nomination

author: Josh Sisco
description: The US Justice Department unconditionally cleared the $3.5 billion deal for Nexstar Media Group Inc. to acquire rival Tegna Inc., which would create the largest operator of local TV stations in the country, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Nexstar’s $3.5 Billion Tegna Deal Cleared by Justice Department

author: Ben Bartenstein, Jennifer A Dlouhy, Samy Adghirni
description: With a fifth of global oil paralyzed, a chaotic campaign against Tehran leaves the White House scrambling to shield the US economy.
title: Iran Leaves an Isolated Trump Grappling With Historic Oil Crisis

author: Michael Hirtzer
description: A bipartisan group of US Senators introduced a bill that would require mandatory price reporting of fertilizer — a bid for more market information after the war in Iran prompted the biggest surge in crop nutrient costs in years.
title: US Senators Call for Fertilizer Price Transparency as Costs Soar

author: Chris Strohm
description: The Justice Department sent a subpoena to former FBI Director James Comey as part of an investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials waged a years-long conspiracy against President Donald Trump, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Justice Department Subpoenas Comey in Trump Conspiracy Probe

author: Magdalena Del Valle, David Gura
description: Removing Miguel Diaz-Canel as president of Cuba to appease the US is out of the question, the country’s ambassador to the United Nations said, adding that talks between the two countries should be based on “mutual respect.”
title: Cuban Envoy Says Current Leaders Will Remain Despite US Pressure

author: Daniel Flatley
description: The Treasury Department added Cuba to a list of countries restricted from taking delivery of Russian oil after a tanker of the fuel appeared to be headed to the island, which is under a US naval blockade.
title: Treasury Says Cuba Can’t Get Russian Oil as Ship Heads to Island

description: Removing Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel in order to appease the US is out of the question, and talks between the two countries should be based on “mutual respect,” said Cuban United Nations Ambassador Ernesto Soberón Guzmán. He speaks exclusively to Bloomberg's David Gura in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Cuba Won't Remove Its President to Appease Trump, Says UN Envoy

description: Has Iran mined the Strait of Hormuz? The oil business has to assume so – which could signal a slow rebound for global energy supplies, Bloomberg’s global defense editor, Gerry Doyle, tells the Big Take podcast’s David Gura. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Iran Mine Threat Rattling Global Oil

author: Brian Platt
description: Before Canada’s election last year, Conservative Party Leader Pierre Poilievre turned down an invitation to appear on the world’s most popular podcast, The Joe Rogan Experience. Rogan had recently endorsed President Donald Trump, who turned Canada’s election upside-down with tariffs and his suggestions the country should be a US state.
title: Carney’s Rival Meets Joe Rogan to Sell Free Trade to the Manosphere

author: Marissa Newman
description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday said Israel would avoid future attacks on Iran’s energy infrastructure, after a pair of strikes on key Middle East gas operations sent energy prices soaring.
title: Israel Will Avoid Attacking Iran’s Energy Assets, Netanyahu Says

author: Alex Vasquez, Gonzalo Soto
description: Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum sent a bill to Congress aimed at promoting public and private investment in strategic infrastructure, at a time when her government is pushing to lure capital to stimulate sluggish economic growth.
title: Sheinbaum Proposes Bill to Bolster Infrastructure Investment

author: Joe Sobczyk
description: Rising energy prices cause an economic pinch as the military seeks extra funds.
title: Iran War Costs Adding Up for Consumers and for the Pentagon

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: Two FBI agents who investigated attempts to overturn the 2020 presidential election and were later fired by the Trump administration are suing to get their jobs back.
title: FBI Agents Sue for Reinstatement Claiming Firing Was Political

author: Liam Knox
description: The Trump administration is transferring management of the $1.7 trillion federal student loan portfolio from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury, the most significant step yet in the White House’s efforts to dismantle a cabinet-level agency.
title: Trump Shifts Federal Student Loan Management From Education Department

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Sheila Kahyaoglu, Managing Director in Equity Research at Jefferies about what the Iran war means for defense companies. Ruth Liao, a Bloomberg News reporter on the impact of the conflict on liquid natural gas. Matt Diczok, Head of Fixed Income Strategy for Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank, discusses the impact on the macro environment. Finally, r. Susan Loeb-Zeitlin, Assistant Professor of Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology discusses how the medical community handles menopause. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pentagon Seeks $200 Billion for Iran | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/19/2026

author: Nick Wadhams
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is circumventing Congress to fast-track the sale up to $16.5 billion in air defense systems, radars and missiles to Middle East allies that have borne the brunt of Iranian retaliation to the US and Israeli military campaign against the regime in Tehran.
title: US Will Fast-Track $16.5 Billion in Weapons to Mideast Allies

author: Paige Smith, Saleha Mohsin, Evan Weinberger, Daniel Flatley
description: Longtime Treasury employees are pushing back against the Trump administration’s plan to make banks verify citizenship information, amid stiff opposition from lenders.
title: Banks, Treasury Staff Push Back on Citizen-Verification Proposal

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss President Donald Trump's meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. On today's show, Democratic Congressman Sam Liccardo of California, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former US Ambassador to NATO Kurt Volker. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Attacks Energy Sites | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/19/2026

author: Saleha Mohsin, Chris Strohm, Josh Wingrove, Joshua Green
description: Top leaders at the Justice Department are rallying behind a US attorney’s efforts to investigate Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and the White House isn’t opposing it, amping up the high-stakes clash with major implications for who will lead the central bank.
title: DOJ, White House Clear Way for Pirro to Keep Powell Probe Going

author: Jim Wyss
description: Ever since US Special Forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro on Jan. 3 and launched an attack on Iran, Washington has been warning that Cuba will be next. Under a US-imposed economic blockade, the island hasn’t received fuel in more than three months, according to Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel.
title: Can Cuba’s Regime Survive as US Chokes Oil Supplies?

author: Ellen Milligan
description: The UK’s large-scale cut to its aid budget will fall on some of the world’s poorest and most unstable countries, as campaigners and Members of Parliament warn of Britain’s declining soft power.
title: UK Foreign Aid Cuts Outstrip Trump’s With Poorest Countries Hit

description: President Donald Trump says the Pentagon request for $200 billion in military funding is "very judicious." He says the US has an unlimited supply of armaments. He speaks in the Oval Office. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says We Have Unlimited Supply of Armaments

author: Eliyahu Kamisher
description: California lawmakers said they will seek to rename upcoming César Chavez Day as Farmworkers Day, after a series of sexual abuse allegations surfaced against the late labor leader.
title: California to Rename César Chavez Holiday After Sex Abuse Claims

description: Bloomberg Tyler Kendall reports on the meeting between President Donald Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the White House. Trump says Japan has stepped up in helping with the Iran war. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Has Warm Welcome For Japanese PM Takaichi

author: Ari Natter
description: The White House is not considering putting restrictions on the export of oil and gas, a Trump administration official said Thursday, following a meeting between Vice President JD Vance and oil executives.
title: White House Not Planning to Ban Oil, Gas Exports, Official Says

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump said his postponed trip to China for a summit with counterpart Xi Jinping had been “reset” and suggested it would take place in mid-May.
title: Trump Says China Meeting ‘Reset’ After Delay Amid Iran War

author: Ellen Milligan, Golnar Motevalli, Alex Wickham
description: Europe’s biggest naval powers don’t see a way of reopening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping before the Iran war subsides.
title: US Allies See No Way of Opening Hormuz Strait During War

author: Jeff Mason, Alastair Gale, Kate Sullivan
description: Tensions between the US and Japan over the Iran war remained evident as President Donald Trump hosted Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, even as he praised Japan for answering his call for support in the effort.
title: Trump Raises Pearl Harbor With Japanese Leader at White House

author: Tom Maloney, Dylan Sloan, Advait Palepu, Pui Gwen Yeung
description: The conflict with Iran, now in its 20th day, highlights a years-long surge in global military spending that’s driving a boom in defense stocks and racking up billions in gains for owners.
title: Soaring Military Spending Adds $28 Billion to Defense Fortunes

author: Clara Hernanz Lizarraga
description: Ángel Escribano ended takeover talks between Indra Sistemas SA, where he is chairman, and EM&E, the firm he owns with his brother, after the government said the deal presented a conflict of interest.
title: Indra Chairman Seeks to End Government Fight, Shelves Deal

author: Dan Williams, Ethan Bronner
description: Israeli officials are riding out a rare public rebuke from US President Donald Trump over the handling of the Iran war, a break from previously tight military coordination between the two allies.
title: Israel Shrugs Off Trump’s Rebuke Over Attack on Iran Gas Field

author: Martha Viotti Beck
description: Brazil Finance Minister Fernando Haddad said he will step down on Thursday, before an April deadline for officials to leave their positions to run for elected office.
title: Brazil Finance Minister Fernando Haddad Steps Down Ahead of Elections

author: Jamie Tarabay
description: Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren called on Kevin Warsh, Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, to explain references to him in Justice Department files on disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
title: Warren Presses Fed Chair Nominee Warsh on Epstein Ties

author: Gerry Doyle
description: At least 16 US military aircraft have been destroyed since the start of the war with Iran, including 10 Reaper strike drones hit by enemy fire, with a half-dozen other planes badly damaged in attacks or accidents.
title: US Aircraft Losses Mount Amid High-Tempo Airstrike Campaign

author: Myles Miller, Magdalena Del Valle
description: US spy chief Tulsi Gabbard acknowledged the US and Israel have different goals for their joint military campaign in Iran, underscoring tensions after Israeli jets struck energy facilities and President Donald Trump pressed for de-escalation.
title: Spy Chief Gabbard Says US, Israel Have Different Iran War Goals

author: Craig Stirling, Mark Schroers, Daniel Hornak
description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde urged governments not to go overboard on help for voters to weather the surge in energy prices, pleading fiscal restraint.
title: Lagarde Warns Europe’s Governments to Keep Lid on Energy Aid

author: Jorge Valero, Ewa Krukowska
description: European Union leaders on Thursday couldn’t break the deadlock over a €90 billion ($103 billion) loan to Ukraine, leaving some fuming over Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s refusal to budge until he regains access to Russian oil.
title: EU Leaders Fail to Unlock Key Ukraine Aid After Orban Digs In

description: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey says it was appropriate to keep interest rate on hold at 3.75% on Thursday due to the situation in the Middle East. There has been a "huge increase in uncertainty," Bailey said in a pooled interview clip. "None of us know how this is going to play out." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: BOE's Bailey Says Appropriate to Hold Rates Amid Iran Uncertainty

description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said inflation risks are skewed to the upside. "A prolonged war in the Middle East could lead to a larger and longer-lasting upward shift in energy prices than currently expected, raising euro-area inflation further," Lagarde said. She was speaking to reporters in Frankfurt following the central bank's decision to keep interest rates on hold on Thursday.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Inflation Risks Tilted to the Upside, ECB's Lagarde Says

description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde says the risks to the euro-area growth outlook are "tilted to the downside," citing heightened uncertainty amid the US-Israel war with Iran. She made the comments during a news conference in Frankfurt after policymakers left interest rates unchanged for a sixth straight meeting.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lagarde Says ECB Sees Downside Risks to Growth Outlook

author: Lorelei Smillie
description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the partial government shutdown will lead to airport closures as challenges grow for Transportation Security Administration agents who are not receiving paychecks.
title: Duffy Says Small Airports Will Close If DHS Shutdown Continues

author: Alex Morales
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer joined counterparts in Japan, Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands in calling on Iran to stop attacks on energy sites and other civilian infrastructure and to end the shipping gridlock in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: UK Joins Allies in Urging Iran to Stop Attacks, Hormuz Gridlock

author: Molly Smith
description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics has shrunk since Brett Matsumoto left it a year ago – but the job he’s poised to take on is bigger than ever.
title: Trump’s New Data Chief Will Face Intense Scrutiny and a Shrunken Workforce

author: Joe Mayes
description: The UK’s city minister will visit European capitals next week in a push to deepen ties with the European Union on financial services as Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves seeks to spur economic growth domestically.
title: UK to Seek Closer Financial Ties With EU as Reeves Chases Growth

author: Alicia Diaz
description: President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Department of Homeland Security advanced through a Senate committee Thursday despite opposition from the panel’s chair, Rand Paul, who argued nominee Markwayne Mullin’s “anger issues” made him unfit to lead an agency under fire for aggressive tactics.
title: Trump DHS Pick Mullin Confirmation Advances Through Senate Panel

description: The European Central Bank kept interest rates unchanged at 2% as officials seek clarity on how damaging the Middle East conflict will prove for inflation and the economy. Bloomberg's Jana Randow reports from Frankfurt. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: ECB Holds Rates as Officials Weigh Impact of Iran War

author: Sanne Wass
description: Denmark’s Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said US President Donald Trump still wants to acquire Greenland, after a report revealed the extent of Copenhagen’s preparations earlier this year to militarily counter a potential US attack.
title: Danish Leader Says Trump Still Wants Greenland as Talks Underway

author: Kamil Kowalcze
description: Germany’s Finance Ministry is considering options for a windfall tax on oil companies that would capture a share of profits driven by surging crude prices as the US-led war on Iran roils markets.
title: Germany Weighs Windfall Tax as Iran War Drives Fuel Price Surge

description: US initial jobless claims fell by 8,000 to 205,000 in the week ending March 14. That is the lowest level since January. Michael McKee reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Jobless Claims Fall to Lowest Level Since January

author: Anthony Halpin
description: A longtime pro-Kremlin activist known for attacks on Russian opposition leader Alexey Navalny lashed out at Vladimir Putin, the latest sign of fatigue with the war on Ukraine.
title: Kremlin Loyalist Turns on Putin as Russians Start to Tire of War

author: Maria Eloisa Capurro
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s decision to potentially stay on at the US central bank after his term as chair expires in May would go against historic norms.
title: Powell Staying at Fed Goes Against Historic Norms, Bessent Says

description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pushed back Thursday against criticism the US war on Iran risked becoming a military “quagmire,” during a press conference at the Pentagon. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War Not Becoming a ‘Quagmire’ or ‘Forever War,’ Hegseth Says

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are set to announce a nuclear power project in the southern US, the latest initiative stemming from an investment fund the countries established as part of a trade pact.
title: Trump, Takaichi Set to Announce $40 Billion US Reactor Project

author: Magan Crane
description: Senator Elizabeth Warren threw her support behind Democratic populist Graham Platner’s effort to unseat Republican Senator Susan Collins.
title: Warren Endorses Platner in Fight to Flip Maine Senate Seat

description: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves discusses Brexit, saying she respects the referendum result but rejects rejoining the European Union. Reeves also outlines her vision for making Britain a Global hub for investment, talent and entrepreneurship-positioning the UK as a "magnet" for wealth. She's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded January 21 on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: There Is No Appetite for Another Brexit Referendum, Reeves Says

description:
Benedetta Berti, Secretary General of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, says NATO is learning many lessons from both the conflict in the Middle East and the Russian invasion of Ukraine, including the need to surge production of defence capabilities in a cost-effective way. Berti was speaking on Bloomberg's The Pulse with Francine Lacqua. 

 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NATO's Berti: We Need Cheaper Ways To Shoot Drones

author: Anthony Capaccio, Courtney McBride
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pushed back against criticism the US war on Iran risked becoming a military “quagmire,” as Iranian attacks on energy infrastructure pushed energy prices even higher on Thursday.
title: Hegseth Says Iran War Not Becoming a ‘Forever War’ or ‘Quagmire’

author: Thomas Seal
description: Canada will buy as many as 65,000 assault rifles to replenish its aging arsenal in a deal with Colt Canada Corp., the latest in a military spending bonanza as the country re-arms.
title: Canada Replaces Army’s 35-Year-Old Rifles in Defense Spending Spree

description: All nine members of the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee voted to leave interest rates unchanged at 3.75% on Thursday. The unanimous vote is the MPC’s first decision without any dissent in four and a half years. Bloomberg’s Jonathan Ferro and Lisa Abramowicz discuss.
title: BOE Votes 9-0 to Keep Rates on Hold

author: Rajesh Roy
description: Ukraine has lodged a protest with Indian authorities over the detention of six of its nationals for allegedly traveling to the restive northeastern region without valid documents and engaging in unlawful activities, its foreign ministry said.
title: Ukraine Lodges Protests Over India’s Detention of Its Citizens

description: Swiss National Bank President Martin Schlegel discusses the central bank’s decision to leave the benchmark interest rate at zero on Thursday. Speaking to Bloomberg News, he restated the SNB’s increased willingness to intervene in the FX market “in order to dampen abrupt and excessive exchange rate movements” to ensure price stability in the country. Schlegel also discusses the current private credit situation, saying it is “not alarming” as the size of private credit in Switzerland is “rather sm
title: SNB’s Schlegel on Rate Decision, FX, Private Credit

author: Ott Tammik
description: A SU-30 Russian military fighter jet entered Estonian airspace for three minutes on Wednesday without posing a serious security threat, the Estonian foreign minister said.
title: Estonia Says Russian Military Jet Violated Its Airspace

author: Ethan Bronner
description: Polls in Israel show overwhelming support for the conflict.
title: Iran War Causes Trump Woes. Not So Netanyahu

author: Andrea Palasciano, Jan Bratanic, Max Ramsay
description: Leaders from the European Union stepped up criticism of Donald Trump’s war in Iran in a clear indication they don’t plan to heed the US president’s demand for allies to help America’s military secure the Strait of Hormuz while fighting continues.
title: European Leaders Harden Stance Against Trump’s ‘Pointless’ War

author: Andrea Dudik, Marton Kasnyik
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban defied pressure from European allies to unlock aid for Ukraine, saying he won’t budge until oil flows from Russia are restored.
title: Defiant Orban Tells EU He Won’t Back Down From Ukraine Aid Veto

author: Sanne Wass
description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen’s party holds a clear lead in polls ahead of next week’s general election shaped by her standoff with US President Donald Trump over Greenland.
title: Danish Premier’s Social Democrats Lead Polls Ahead of Election

author: Ruth Liao, Stephen Stapczynski, Priscila Azevedo Rocha
description: The industry is staring down prolonged disruptions in the Persian Gulf. Emerging economies are already paying the price.
title: Weeks of War Are Reshaping the Global Gas Market for Years to Come

author: Adveith Nair
description: The United Arab Emirates’ ambassador to the US threw his weight behind his country’s massive investment plans in America, amid concerns that a prolonged war with Iran could strain government finances across the Persian Gulf.
title: UAE Stands by $1.4 Trillion US Investment Pledge Despite War

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: Romania’s ruling coalition reached an agreement in budget negotiations after the dominant Social Democrats pushed through parts of a spending package that had stalled the talks.
title: Romanian Coalition Secures Deal to Move Forward Stalled Budget

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Parliament’s trade committee advanced the bloc’s trade deal with the US, setting it up for a final vote despite lingering uncertainty about the tariff regime for EU exports.
title: EU Moves Forward in Approving Trade Agreement With US

author: Wes Kosova
description: An estimated $11 billion was spent in just the first six days.
title: The Enormous Financial Cost of Three Weeks of War in Iran

description: A Qatari complex housing the world’s largest liquefied natural gas export plant suffered “extensive damage” following a strike by an Iranian missile. The Ras Laffan Industrial City, home to the LNG plant that accounted for about a fifth of global supply before production was halted earlier this month, was hit after four other missiles were intercepted, authorities said late Wednesday. Bloomberg's Anthony di Paola reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Qatar LNG Plant Suffers 'Extensive Damage' After Iran Strike

author: Patrick Sykes, Dana Khraiche
description: US President Donald Trump sought to stop attacks on energy facilities in the Middle East after Israel and Iran struck key targets, fueling concern that a prolonged war will cause lasting damage to oil and gas infrastructure.
title: Trump Seeks End to Attacks on Energy Sites as Gas Fields Burn

description:
On today's show, US President Donald Trump pressed for a de-escalation of attacks on Middle East energy sites. He said Israel will refrain from further strikes on the South Pars gas field and threatened retaliation if there are more attacks by Iran on Qatar’s LNG facilities.

Jerome Powell says higher energy prices will push up overall inflation in the near term, but it’s too soon to know the potential effects on the economy. The Fed kept rates on hold as expected.

The ECB is projected to hold rates steady, with traders fully pricing two hikes later this year amid the threat of rising inflation. The BOE is also set to stand pat.

Today's guests: Bank of America Greater China Chief Economist Helen Qiao (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Calls for De-Escalation on Mideast Energy Site Attacks | Daybreak Europe 3/19/2026

description: European Union leaders are meeting in Brussels, where they plan to discuss the upheaval in the Middle East and the issue of bolstering the bloc’s competitiveness. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook discusses what to expect.
title: Iran War to Dominate EU Leaders’ Summit in Brussels

description: The European Central Bank and the Bank of England are both expected to keep interest rates unchanged on Thursday, as officials assess the disruption caused by the conflict in the Middle East. The ECB is expected to hold the deposit rate at 2% and the BOE’s Monetary Policy Committee is expected to keep the benchmark rate on hold at 3.75%. Bloomberg’s Jana Randow and Morwenna Coniam break down the situation.
title: ECB and BOE Expected to Keep Interest Rates on Hold

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: North Korea’s foreign currency earnings have reached their highest levels since before sweeping sanctions were imposed in 2018 over its banned weapons programs, driven by cyber-heists and arms sales to Russia, US intelligence authorities said.
title: North Korea FX Revenue Boosted by Russia Arms Sales, Cyber Crime

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Anutin Charnvirakul won a parliamentary vote Thursday for a new term as Thailand’s prime minister, clearing the way for the conservative politician to form a cabinet that faces the immediate challenge of managing the fallout from the war in the Middle East.
title: Thai PM Anutin Tightens Grip on Power by Securing New Term

author: Helen Nyambura
description: Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda agreed to “de-escalate tensions” and implement a peace agreement reached with the help of US President Donald Trump last year.
title: Congo, Rwanda Agree to Ease Tensions After Washington Talks

description:
Sanae Takaichi is making her first trip to Washington as Japan's leader with a question hanging over how far Tokyo will be pushed to contribute to efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg Opinion's Gearoid Reidy shares his views.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Opinion: Takaichi Will Walk a Diplomatic Tightrope in US

author: Myles Miller
description: The FBI has opened an investigation into former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent over alleged unauthorized disclosures of classified information, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: FBI Probes Former Counterterror Chief Joe Kent in Leak Inquiry

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Joseph Lavorgna, SMBC Americas Chief Economist, states “they did what they were suppose to do” when sharing his thoughts on the Federal Reserve opting to keep interest rates steady. Nadhim Zahawi, former UK Chancellor of the Exchequer, shares his thoughts on President Trump criticizing UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer for not being more supportive of the US’ efforts when it comes to Iran. Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin (R) discusses the rising cost of US involvement in Iran, the ongoing DHS funding standoff, and the path forward for the SAVE America Act. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Projects One Rate Cut in 2026 | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/18/2026

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: Congressional Democrats walked out of a briefing with US Attorney General Pam Bondi and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche that was intended to cover the Justice Department’s handling of files related to sex trafficking investigations of disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
title: House Democrats Walk Out of Bondi Briefing on Epstein Files
